claims.statement: mise.toml sets UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT to ~/.local/share/harnessed/venvs/<branch>/.venv, keeping the venv per-git-branch and outside the repository so a podman container bind-mounting the repo cannot corrupt it — with the consequence that a fresh worktree starts with no venv and does not inherit main's.

tools/run-tests.sh is the sanctioned way to invoke the suite because it absorbs three traps that fail locally while CI stays green: the per-branch venv outside the repo, pytest being an optional extra whose absence makes `uv run pytest` silently fall through to a system pytest erroring with ModuleNotFoundError, and mise's untrusted-config refusal in a new worktree (handled by an upfront `mise trust`).

The suite must never be invoked as bare pytest or a hand-composed mise/uv/pytest line: tools/run-tests.sh forwards pytest arguments (whole suite, one file, `-k` filters, `-x`), and CI is held to the same entry point — live.yml invokes `tools/run-tests.sh -v` with HARNESSED_PODMAN=1, and tests/test_live_workflow.py fails the workflow definition if it hand-composes a pytest line, so a local green and a CI green are evidence about the same thing by construction.

mise is a hard prerequisite, not an optional convenience: tools/run-tests.sh shells out to mise on its first line and fails with 'is mise installed and on PATH?' without it, and mise.toml's [tools] declares the pinned pyright and shellcheck that the lint layers run — so neither lint layer can execute without mise (tools/preflight.sh reports them as skipped by name instead).

mise.toml pins UV_PYTHON to 3.12, the floor of requires-python (>=3.12) and what CI's default job runs, because an unpinned uv picks the newest interpreter on the box so no local run exercises the supported version — which hid a real catalogseed crash (Path.resolve() raising on a failing readlink under 3.12, swallowed under 3.13) through a full local review (bd harnessed-925); CI covers the top of the range with a separate pytest-py313 job.

tools/preflight.sh replays every CI gate in CI's order — pytest, then ruff, then pyright, then shellcheck — because lint.yml has no continue-on-error and ruff is first, so on CI a ruff finding means pyright and shellcheck never ran and a red lint job understates what is unverified (this happened on PR #431: two RUF005 findings with pytest fully green).

tools/preflight.sh takes two flags: --all additionally runs the catalog pin check (`harnessed update --check`, opt-in locally because it queries live release feeds over the network and is irrelevant to changes that do not touch catalog/), and --no-tests runs only the lint layers for a docs- or shell-only change; CI runs the pin check on a weekly Monday-06:00-UTC schedule rather than per-PR because a live-registry result would fail unrelated branches through nobody's fault.

preflight's one deliberate divergence from CI: every gate runs even after an earlier one fails, and each layer that did not run is reported by name in the summary — CI stops at the first failure and leaves the rest unverified silently, whereas preflight hands over the whole list in one pass and never prints a bare 'all gates passed' while a layer was skipped.

pyright must be given the venv interpreter explicitly (preflight resolves it from the same uv venv and passes --pythonpath, matching lint.yml): because mise.toml puts the venv outside the repo and activates it via _.source, a bare pyright inherits no activation, resolves none of the installed packages, and reports hundreds of phantom reportMissingImports on a tree that is genuinely clean.

`mise run openwiki-drift` runs tools/openwiki-drift.py — no model call, no network — which recomputes each Claim's line-ranged evidence digest and exits 0 when nothing changed, 1 when at least one Claim's cited code changed or its file is gone, and 2 when the wiki or its Claims are unreadable or malformed; it is the cheap check to run before trusting or regenerating any wiki page.

The drift gate verifies only evidence carrying a repo://path#L<a>-L<b> range: whole-file evidence (no range to hash) and unknown version schemes are counted and reported as skipped, never verified; and it separates a moved-but-identical block from a genuinely changed one (27.5% moved vs 4.7% changed measured over a one-week window), so a green run means 'nothing it cites has moved', not 'everything it says is true'.

harnessed has two console entrypoints with one division of labor: `harnessed` (harnessed.launcher:main, a Typer app) owns every verb that can touch the container runtime, launch an agent, or manage host-side state; `harnessed-tools` (harnessed.cli:main, argparse) is the emit-only/analysis surface (assemble, persist-list/persist-prune, lint-prose, scan-image-online) plus `test`, which launches a headless instance and therefore needs podman/docker.

launcher.main rewrites argv before Typer parses it: it splits passthrough args off at the first standalone `--` (appending them verbatim to the harness command of whichever run verb fires) and enforces that the leading token is always a subcommand — there is no bare-stack shortcut, because the earlier 'stack name unless it matches a registered command' design made every new verb require a hand-maintained registration and read its failures as usage errors (`harnessed update` parsing as a launch and failing with Missing argument 'HARNESS').

`harnessed container-run` and `harnessed host-run` hand the terminal to a live agent session and are not for automation: both end by replacing the launcher process — os.execvp hands the TTY to the runtime attach on the container path, os.execvpe execs the harness against the real home on the host path — so nothing can observe or reap the session afterward; the ban is stated in AGENTS.md (mirrored in CLAUDE.md), and `harnessed build`, `harnessed test`, `harnessed list`, or reading the source are the ways to reason about behavior.

`harnessed test <stack> <harness>` is the headless equivalent of a launch: the launcher verb delegates to capability.py, which runs `container-run <harness> <project> --stack <name> --fresh` with HARNESSED_HEADLESS=true — pod up with no interactive attach — introspects the live instance against the manifest-derived oracle, and tears the instance down as part of the contract; it also auto-assembles first when the profile is missing or stale.

podman or docker is required only for live work — the live layer behind HARNESSED_PODMAN=1, `harnessed test`, and `container-run` — while the hermetic pytest suite and harnessed-tools' emit-only verbs (assemble never invokes podman/docker) run with no container runtime installed; _runtime() prefers podman, falls back to docker, and exits when neither is on PATH.

A green hermetic suite run proves no container behavior: it performs no podman build and no harnessed container-run, the HARNESSED_PODMAN-gated tests skip on a podman-less runner (with conftest printing a 'live verification' section naming what did not execute — a skip is not a pass), and the gated layer's only home is live.yml on push-to-main plus a nightly cron, deliberately never on pull requests.

The live layer is fail-closed about its own gate: tests/conftest.py's pytest_sessionfinish fails the run when HARNESSED_PODMAN=1 is set and any live_podman-marked test skipped anyway, and that decision keys on the marker rather than on skip wording — two earlier wording-based versions failed in opposite directions (missing image-precondition skips, or failing on unrelated platform/optional-dependency skips) — so a broken podman cannot masquerade as success.

A safe first end-to-end slice is `tools/run-tests.sh`, then `harnessed build default claude`, then `harnessed test default claude`: `default` is the shipped baseline stack (one recipe, no services, no policy fields) that every dynamic --recipe stack extends, the suite needs no runtime, and build/test exercise the real images the hermetic suite never touches.

The baseline test count must be recorded before a change: a drop is a regression even if the new tests pass, because a suite of this size hides a silently deselected file behind any green tick and the count is the only signal that catches it.

mise's openwiki tasks are split by cost so the drift check can run anywhere: [tasks.openwiki-drift] is non-interactive with no varlock, no model, and no credential (it only executes tools/openwiki-drift.py and signals via exit status), whereas openwiki-update, openwiki-init, and openwiki-chat are interactive = true and reach the generator through vars.openwiki_env — an `env -u` stripping of provider exports wrapped in `varlock run` against ~/.config/harnessed — because those tasks talk to a model; openwiki-visualize needs no credential either, but only serves local Markdown.

mise.toml's [tools] block declares and pins the four non-Python tools the dev loop and the wiki tasks depend on — shellcheck 0.11.0, npm:pyright 1.1.411, npm:varlock 1.16.1, and npm:openwiki 0.4.3 — rather than assuming them on PATH; the npm:openwiki entry additionally requires two escape hatches or the install fails in ways that do not look like packaging problems: trust_policy_excludes (fastq ships no provenance attestation at 1.20.2, so the no-downgrade trust policy refuses the whole install) and allow_builds (the mise install backend denies dependency lifecycle scripts by default, and better-sqlite3's install script is what produces better_sqlite3.node — denied, the install still reports success and every openwiki run dies at 'Could not locate the bindings file').

mise's openwiki tasks must be run from the main checkout, not a task worktree: docs/ is a gitignored live clone of the GitHub wiki, so a worktree checkout does not have it and a wiki run from there would be generated from an incomplete view of the project's own documentation.
